concepts.title: Venture capital schemes
concepts.hook: VC: 50 investors max · 250k ticket · 3M–200M corpus · 80% in 10 years.

concepts.title: Restricted schemes
concepts.hook: Restricted: 1,000 investors max · 150k ticket (40k staff) · 3M corpus.
concepts.tricky: VC ticket is 250k; Restricted is 150k. Staff: 60k vs 40k. Easy to swap.

concepts.title: Retail schemes
concepts.hook: Retail: file 21 working days ahead · 20 investors · no one above 25%.
concepts.tricky: Retail extension needs 2/3 investors AND the Authority. Restricted needs only 2/3.

concepts.title: Special situation funds
concepts.hook: SSF: close-ended ONLY · 3 years min · ONE 6-month extension at 50% fee.
concepts.tricky: Restricted schemes got the multi-extension regime in 2026. SSF did NOT — still one-time.

concepts.title: ETFs & commodity ETFs
concepts.hook: Gold/Silver ETF: 90% in the metal, ETCD capped at 10%.

concepts.title: Custody, valuation & reporting
concepts.hook: Custody triggers: Retail · open-ended Restricted · AUM above USD 70M.

concepts.title: Approved & coming (July 2026)
concepts.hook: Approved 24 Jul 2026 — NOT notified. The 30 Jan 2026 text still binds.
concepts.tricky: Approval sets direction; notification sets obligation.

questions.question: The IFSCA FME framework recognises which categories of Fund Management Entities?
questions.option_A: Authorised FME, Registered FME (Non-Retail) and Registered FME (Retail)
questions.option_B: Category I FME, Category II FME and Category III FME, mirroring the AIF regime
questions.option_C: Authorised FME, Registered FME and Exempted FME, based on the investors served
questions.option_D: Authorised FME (Retail), Authorised FME (Non-Retail) and Branch FME
questions.correct_text: Authorised FME, Registered FME (Non-Retail) and Registered FME (Retail)
questions.explanation: Reg. 4 creates three categories in an ascending ladder: Authorised, Registered (Non-Retail), Registered (Retail). Each higher category can also undertake everything permitted to the ones below it.

questions.question: An Authorised FME is permitted to:
questions.option_A: Launch Venture Capital Schemes and restricted schemes, and offer Portfolio Management Services
questions.option_B: Launch Venture Capital Schemes for accredited/threshold investors, and manage a Family Investment Fund for a Single Family
questions.option_C: Launch retail schemes and exchange traded funds, and manage a Family Investment Fund for a Single Family
questions.option_D: Manage a Family Investment Fund for several unrelated families, and act as investment manager for private placements
questions.correct_text: Launch Venture Capital Schemes for accredited/threshold investors, and manage a Family Investment Fund for a Single Family
questions.explanation: The Authorised FME tier covers two activities: VC schemes via private placement to accredited investors or those above the threshold, and Family Investment Funds set up by a Single Family. Everything else needs registration.

questions.question: In addition to restricted schemes and everything an Authorised FME can do, a Registered FME (Non-Retail) may:
questions.option_A: Offer Portfolio Management Services (including for a multi-family office) and act as investment manager for public offers of REITs and InvITs
questions.option_B: Launch exchange traded funds and retail schemes, and act as investment manager for private placements of REITs and InvITs
questions.option_C: Offer Portfolio Management Services (including for a multi-family office) and act as investment manager for private placements of REITs and InvITs
questions.option_D: Manage a Family Investment Fund for a Single Family and offer Portfolio Management Services to accredited investors only
questions.correct_text: Offer Portfolio Management Services (including for a multi-family office) and act as investment manager for private placements of REITs and InvITs
questions.explanation: The Non-Retail tier adds PMS (including multi-family office) and IM roles for privately placed Investment Trusts. Public offers of REITs/InvITs and ETFs remain exclusive to the Retail tier.

questions.question: Which activities are exclusive to a Registered FME (Retail)?
questions.option_A: Launching restricted schemes and ETFs, and acting as investment manager for private placements of REITs and InvITs
questions.option_B: Launching Venture Capital Schemes, and acting as investment manager for public offers of REITs and InvITs
questions.option_C: Offering Portfolio Management Services, and acting as investment manager for public offers of Investment Trusts
questions.option_D: Launching retail schemes and ETFs, and acting as investment manager for public offers of REITs and InvITs
questions.correct_text: Launching retail schemes and ETFs, and acting as investment manager for public offers of REITs and InvITs
questions.explanation: Retail is the apex tier: retail schemes, ETFs, and IM for publicly offered Investment Trusts — plus everything permitted to the two lower categories.

questions.question: The minimum net worth for a Registered FME (Retail) is:
questions.explanation: Second Schedule ladder: Authorised FME USD 75,000; Registered (Non-Retail) USD 500,000; Registered (Retail) USD 1,000,000. Note Reg. 8(1): compliance is "at all times", not just at registration.

questions.question: An FME operating as a branch in IFSC satisfies the minimum net worth requirement:
questions.option_A: By ring-fencing the full amount in a bank account maintained with a banking unit in the IFSC
questions.option_B: At the parent level, with the parent ensuring adequate funds for the branch's day-to-day operations
questions.option_C: At the parent level, provided the parent is regulated in a jurisdiction having an arrangement with IFSCA
questions.option_D: At the branch level only, computed separately from the parent and certified by its auditors annually
questions.correct_text: At the parent level, with the parent ensuring adequate funds for the branch's day-to-day operations
questions.explanation: Reg. 8(2): branch structures maintain net worth at the parent level, but the parent must ensure adequate operational funding for the branch. Reg. 8(3) adds that FME net worth is separate from and additional to net worth required for other activities.

questions.question: If IFSCA finds deficiencies in a registration application, the applicant gets:
questions.option_A: Fifteen (15) days to rectify the deficiencies
questions.option_B: Ninety (90) days to rectify the deficiencies
questions.option_C: Thirty (30) days to rectify the deficiencies
questions.option_D: Sixty (60) days to rectify the deficiencies
questions.correct_text: Thirty (30) days to rectify the deficiencies
questions.explanation: Reg. 14(1): deficiencies are communicated with 30 days to cure. Failure to rectify to the Authority's satisfaction lets IFSCA refuse registration with reasons (Reg. 14(2)).

questions.question: A Registered FME (Non-Retail) wants to become a Registered FME (Retail). It:
questions.option_A: May switch on filing an intimation with the Authority within fifteen days
questions.option_B: May switch automatically once it satisfies the higher net worth requirement
questions.option_C: Must surrender its existing certificate and file a fresh application in all cases
questions.option_D: Cannot change category except with the prior approval of the Authority
questions.correct_text: Cannot change category except with the prior approval of the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 13(2): category is fixed at grant; any change requires prior IFSCA approval. Meeting the higher net worth is necessary but not sufficient.

questions.question: A voluntary surrender of an FME's certificate of registration becomes effective:
questions.option_A: Only upon its acceptance by the Authority
questions.option_B: On the date the surrender application is filed with the Authority
questions.option_C: Thirty days after the application is filed, unless objected to
questions.option_D: At the end of the financial year in which it was filed
questions.correct_text: Only upon its acceptance by the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 16 Explanation: surrender is effective only on acceptance by IFSCA — the FME remains regulated (and liable) until then.

questions.question: Module 1 — Numbers Deck
Is this the 2022 framework or the current 2025 framework?
questions.explanation: 2022 framework. The 2025 regulations redesignated the second KMP as "Compliance Officer" — responsible for compliance and for ensuring implementation of risk management policies. The old designation survives as a favourite distractor.

questions.question: Is this the 2022 definition or the current 2025 definition?
questions.explanation: Current 2025 definition. The 2022 text required the officer to be "financially literate and capable of appreciating requirements"; 2025 recast this as "capable of understanding the financial statements and the requirements" — a more concrete competence standard.

questions.question: The Principal Officer of an FME carries overall responsibility for:
questions.option_A: Fund management only, with compliance resting solely with the Compliance Officer
questions.option_B: The activities of the FME including fund management, risk management and compliance
questions.option_C: Marketing, investor relations and distribution of the schemes under management
questions.option_D: Custody and settlement of the assets held by each of the FME's schemes
questions.correct_text: The activities of the FME including fund management, risk management and compliance
questions.explanation: The PO is the apex accountable individual — fund management, risk management and compliance all roll up to this role. The Compliance Officer supports but does not displace PO accountability.

questions.question: Under the 2025 regulations, the additional KMP that every FME must appoint alongside the Principal Officer is designated as:
questions.option_A: Compliance and Risk Manager
questions.option_B: Chief Investment Officer
questions.option_C: Compliance Officer
questions.option_D: Money Laundering Reporting Officer
questions.correct_text: Compliance Officer
questions.explanation: Reg. 7(2): the second mandatory KMP is the Compliance Officer, responsible for regulatory compliance and implementation of risk management policies. "Compliance and Risk Manager" is the superseded 2022 designation.

questions.question: A Registered FME (Retail) must appoint an additional KMP responsible for fund management:
questions.option_A: Within six months of obtaining its certificate of registration from the Authority
questions.option_B: Only once assets under management cross USD 1 billion at a financial year end
questions.option_C: Before launching its tenth scheme, counting both retail and non-retail schemes
questions.option_D: Before filing with the Authority the offer document of its first retail scheme or ETF
questions.correct_text: Before filing with the Authority the offer document of its first retail scheme or ETF
questions.explanation: Reg. 7(3): the fund-management KMP must be in place before the first retail scheme or ETF offer document is filed — a pre-filing gate, not a post-launch obligation.

questions.question: Any FME managing AUM of at least USD 1 billion as at the close of a financial year must appoint an additional fund-management KMP. For this threshold, AUM:
questions.option_A: Excludes the AUM of fund of funds schemes
questions.option_B: Includes all schemes without exception
questions.option_C: Excludes retail schemes
questions.option_D: Is measured as a daily average, not at year-close
questions.correct_text: Excludes the AUM of fund of funds schemes
questions.explanation: Reg. 7(4): the USD 1 billion test is applied at financial year close, excluding FoF scheme AUM — since FoF assets are managed at the underlying scheme level.

questions.question: The "record of fairness and integrity" limb of the fit and proper test expressly includes:
questions.option_A: Minimum net worth, solvency and adequate liquidity at all times
questions.option_B: Financial integrity, good reputation and character, and honesty
questions.option_C: Educational qualifications and prescribed professional certifications
questions.option_D: Ten years of experience in the securities market or fund management
questions.correct_text: Financial integrity, good reputation and character, and honesty
questions.explanation: Reg. 9(2)(a) lists three elements: financial integrity; good reputation and character; honesty. It applies to the applicant, PO, directors/partners, KMPs and controlling shareholders — at all times.

questions.question: The Compliance Officer must report to:
questions.option_A: The Principal Officer, who carries overall responsibility for the FME's activities
questions.option_B: The Authority directly, without routing anything through the FME's management
questions.option_C: The board of directors, or the head of the organisation where there is no board
questions.option_D: The statutory auditor appointed by the fiduciaries of each scheme managed
questions.correct_text: The board of directors, or the head of the organisation where there is no board
questions.explanation: The definition hard-wires independence: the CO reports to the board (or org head absent a board) — not to the PO whose activities the CO monitors.

questions.question: Module 2 — KMP Deck
Is this the 2022 position or the current 2025 position?
questions.explanation: 2022 position — maximum 49 investors ("less than fifty"). The 2025 regulations say "shall not have more than fifty (50)" — maximum 50. A scheme with exactly 50 investors: non-compliant under 2022, compliant under 2025.

questions.question: Under the current 2025 regulations, a non-accredited investor may invest in a Venture Capital scheme by investing:
questions.option_A: Above USD 250,000 — strictly more than the threshold, as under the 2022 regulations
questions.option_B: At least USD 150,000
questions.option_C: Any amount, if the scheme has fewer than 50 investors
questions.option_D: At least USD 250,000 — exactly USD 250,000 qualifies
questions.correct_text: At least USD 250,000 — exactly USD 250,000 qualifies
questions.explanation: 2025 requires "at least USD 250,000", so exactly USD 250,000 qualifies; 2022's "above USD 250,000" excluded it. Employees/directors/designated partners: minimum USD 60,000. USD 150,000 is the lower application size that pushes a scheme into the restricted route.

questions.question: A Venture Capital scheme's corpus must be:
questions.option_A: At least USD 3 Million and not exceeding USD 200 Million
questions.option_B: At least USD 1 Million with no ceiling
questions.option_C: At least USD 5 Million and not exceeding USD 100 Million
questions.option_D: At least USD 3 Million with no ceiling
questions.correct_text: At least USD 3 Million and not exceeding USD 200 Million
questions.explanation: Reg. 23(1) sets both ends: USD 3M minimum, USD 200M maximum. VC is the only mainstream scheme type with a corpus ceiling — target more and you must use the restricted-scheme route.

questions.question: A Venture Capital scheme must invest at least 80% of its corpus in:
questions.option_A: Securities listed on a recognised stock exchange in the IFSC or in any foreign jurisdiction
questions.option_B: Investee companies incorporated not more than ten (10) years ago, or other schemes meeting that requirement
questions.option_C: Investee companies incorporated not more than five (5) years ago, or other schemes meeting that test
questions.option_D: Government securities, money market instruments and other cash equivalents held in the IFSC
questions.correct_text: Investee companies incorporated not more than ten (10) years ago, or other schemes meeting that requirement
questions.explanation: Reg. 23(3): ≥80% of corpus into companies within 10 years of incorporation — the provision that keeps "venture capital" venture. Feeder investment into other compliant schemes also counts.

questions.question: For a VC scheme with targeted corpus up to USD 30 Million, the FME or its associate must invest:
questions.option_A: At least 5% and not more than 10% of the targeted corpus
questions.option_B: A flat USD 750,000
questions.option_C: At least 2.5% and not more than 10% of the targeted corpus
questions.option_D: At least 1% with no upper limit
questions.correct_text: At least 2.5% and not more than 10% of the targeted corpus
questions.explanation: Reg. 28(1)(a): 2.5%–10% band for schemes up to USD 30M targeted corpus. The floor aligns manager incentives; the cap prevents the FME dominating its own fund.

questions.question: For a VC scheme with targeted corpus above USD 30 Million, the FME/associate contribution is:
questions.option_A: At least 2.5% of the targeted corpus, whatever the size
questions.option_B: At least USD 1,500,000, not exceeding 10%
questions.option_C: Waived entirely above USD 30 Million
questions.option_D: At least USD 750,000, not exceeding 10% of the targeted corpus
questions.correct_text: At least USD 750,000, not exceeding 10% of the targeted corpus
questions.explanation: Above USD 30M the floor becomes absolute: USD 750,000 (the 2.5%-of-30M figure frozen), capped at 10%. The contribution is not mandatory for schemes relocated to IFSC from outside India.

questions.question: A VC scheme may invest in an associate of the FME:
questions.option_A: Subject to prior approval of 75% of investors in the scheme by value
questions.option_B: Freely, if disclosed in the placement memorandum
questions.option_C: Never — associate investments are prohibited
questions.option_D: With prior approval of a simple majority of investors by number
questions.correct_text: Subject to prior approval of 75% of investors in the scheme by value
questions.explanation: Reg. 23(2): associate investments need prior approval of 75% of investors by value — the recurring supermajority standard for conflicted transactions across the regulations.

questions.question: The FME must compute the NAV of each Venture Capital scheme:
questions.option_A: Daily, in line with the practice followed for retail schemes
questions.option_B: At least on an annual basis, with fully documented methodology
questions.option_C: Monthly, and disclosed to investors within ten working days
questions.option_D: Only at the time of winding up the scheme and its final distribution
questions.correct_text: At least on an annual basis, with fully documented methodology
questions.explanation: Reg. 27: annual minimum, with the calculation procedure documented, regularly verified and amended where needed. Illiquid venture portfolios don't warrant daily NAVs — but they do demand methodological discipline.

questions.question: The assets of a VC scheme must be valued by an independent service provider, which may be:
questions.option_A: Only a chartered accountant holding a certificate of practice, appointed and rotated by the FME periodically
questions.option_B: The FME's own internal valuation committee, provided that it excludes the scheme's own fund managers
questions.option_C: A fund administrator, a custodian, a credit rating agency registered with the Authority, or an IBBI-registered valuer
questions.option_D: Any merchant banker registered with a securities regulator in India or in a comparable foreign jurisdiction
questions.correct_text: A fund administrator, a custodian, a credit rating agency registered with the Authority, or an IBBI-registered valuer
questions.explanation: Reg. 26(2) lists the eligible independents: fund administrator, custodian, Authority-registered CRA, IBBI-registered valuer, or others as specified. Valuation norms themselves sit in the Sixth Schedule.

questions.question: A Venture Capital scheme may borrow or engage in leverage:
questions.option_A: No — venture capital schemes are strictly prohibited from borrowing or employing leverage of any kind at all
questions.option_B: Only for bridge financing of up to thirty days, and then only against capital committed but not yet called
questions.option_C: Only with the prior approval of the Authority, obtained separately in respect of each individual borrowing
questions.option_D: Yes — subject to conditions including disclosure of maximum leverage and calculation methodology in the placement memorandum
questions.correct_text: Yes — subject to conditions including disclosure of maximum leverage and calculation methodology in the placement memorandum
questions.explanation: Reg. 25 permits leverage on a disclosure-and-conditions basis: the PPM must state the maximum leverage and how it is calculated. The regime trusts disclosure over prohibition.

questions.question: Which joint investors must together invest at least USD 250,000 in a VC scheme?
questions.option_A: An investor with their spouse, parent, or daughter/son
questions.option_B: Any two colleagues from the same employer
questions.option_C: An investor and any relative up to the fourth degree
questions.option_D: Only married couples
questions.correct_text: An investor with their spouse, parent, or daughter/son
questions.explanation: The provisos permit joint investment where the combined amount meets USD 250,000, but only for three pairings: spouse; parent; child. Each other joint investor must independently meet the minimum.

questions.question: Module 3 — VC Numbers Deck
What's wrong here?
questions.option_A: Nothing is wrong — the scheme remains comfortably within the 25% cap on unlisted securities that applies to open-ended restricted schemes
questions.option_B: The 25% cap is satisfied, but post the 2026 Amendment an open-ended scheme cannot touch unlisted securities until it achieves USD 3 Million corpus
questions.option_C: The scheme could not have commenced any investment activity at all until it had first reached the USD 3 Million minimum corpus required
questions.option_D: Open-ended restricted schemes are never permitted to invest in unlisted securities at all, whatever the size of the corpus they have raised
questions.correct_text: The 25% cap is satisfied, but post the 2026 Amendment an open-ended scheme cannot touch unlisted securities until it achieves USD 3 Million corpus

questions.question: A restricted scheme may have at most:
questions.option_A: Fifty (50) investors, matching the venture capital scheme ceiling
questions.option_B: Two hundred (200) investors, in line with the private placement limit
questions.option_C: One thousand (1000) investors, or such number as the Authority specifies
questions.option_D: No limit at all, provided each meets the minimum investment threshold
questions.correct_text: One thousand (1000) investors, or such number as the Authority specifies
questions.explanation: Reg. 32(1): 1000-investor ceiling (subject to Authority variation). The 50-investor cap belongs to VC schemes; retail schemes have no ceiling at all.

questions.question: Among restricted schemes filed as Category I, II and III AIFs, open-ended structure is available to:
questions.option_A: All three categories, at the option of the fund management entity
questions.option_B: Category I and II schemes only, since Category III must be close-ended
questions.option_C: None — every restricted scheme must be filed as a close-ended scheme
questions.option_D: Category III schemes only — Category I and II must be close-ended
questions.correct_text: Category III schemes only — Category I and II must be close-ended
questions.explanation: Reg. 30(2): schemes under clauses (a) and (c) — the Cat I and Cat II routes — file close-ended; only clause (b) schemes (Cat III) may file open- or close-ended.

questions.question: An open-ended restricted scheme may commence investment activities upon raising:
questions.option_A: USD 1 Million, achieving the USD 3 Million minimum corpus within 12 months of the taken-on-record communication
questions.option_B: USD 3 Million in full and upfront, before any investment activity of the scheme may commence
questions.option_C: USD 500,000, with no further corpus milestone applying to the scheme thereafter at all
questions.option_D: USD 2 Million, achieving the USD 3 Million minimum corpus within six months of the launch date
questions.correct_text: USD 1 Million, achieving the USD 3 Million minimum corpus within 12 months of the taken-on-record communication
questions.explanation: The two-step ladder: start at USD 1M, reach USD 3M within 12 months. Post the 2026 Amendment, unlisted securities remain off-limits until USD 3M is achieved.

questions.question: For a close-ended restricted scheme with targeted corpus up to USD 30 Million, the FME/associate must invest:
questions.option_A: At least 5% and not more than 10%
questions.option_B: At least 2.5% and not more than 10% of the targeted corpus
questions.option_C: At least USD 1,500,000
questions.option_D: Nothing — skin in the game applies only to VC schemes
questions.correct_text: At least 2.5% and not more than 10% of the targeted corpus
questions.explanation: Reg. 40(a): close-ended restricted schemes mirror the VC bands — 2.5%–10% up to USD 30M; ≥USD 750,000 (≤10%) above it.

questions.question: For an open-ended restricted scheme, the FME/associate contribution floor is:
questions.option_A: 2.5% of targeted corpus, or USD 750,000 — the same floor as for close-ended schemes
questions.option_B: A flat 1% of assets under management of the scheme, measured at each year end
questions.option_C: 5% of targeted corpus (below USD 30M), or USD 1,500,000 (above USD 30M) — both capped at 10%
questions.option_D: Nil, since open-ended schemes already offer redemption liquidity to investors
questions.correct_text: 5% of targeted corpus (below USD 30M), or USD 1,500,000 (above USD 30M) — both capped at 10%
questions.explanation: Reg. 40(b): open-ended schemes carry double the close-ended floors — 5% / USD 1.5M — reflecting the higher risk manager-investor misalignment poses when investors can redeem.

questions.question: A restricted scheme may buy or sell securities from associates, other schemes of the FME, or an investor committed to 50%+ of the corpus:
questions.option_A: Freely, provided that the transaction is disclosed to the investors after it has been completed
questions.option_B: Never, under any circumstances, whatever approval the investors may be willing to give
questions.option_C: With the prior approval of a simple majority of investors, counting all investors alike
questions.option_D: Only with prior approval of 75% of investors by value — excluding the votes of the 50%+ committed investor
questions.correct_text: Only with prior approval of 75% of investors by value — excluding the votes of the 50%+ committed investor
questions.explanation: Reg. 35(4): conflicted trades need the 75%-by-value supermajority, and the conflicted mega-investor is excluded from the vote — approval must come from the unconflicted.

questions.question: When a restricted scheme co-invests through a segregated portfolio (separate unit class), the segregated portfolio's investment terms must be:
questions.option_A: In no circumstances more favourable than those offered to the common portfolio
questions.option_B: Identical in every respect to the terms offered to the common portfolio
questions.option_C: More favourable, so as to compensate co-investors for the concentration risk
questions.option_D: Left entirely to commercial negotiation between the FME and the co-investors
questions.correct_text: In no circumstances more favourable than those offered to the common portfolio
questions.explanation: Reg. 41(2)(a): co-investors may get access, but never better terms than the main pool — protecting common-portfolio investors from structural subordination. Disclosure in the PPM is also mandatory.

questions.question: An SPV used by a restricted scheme for co-investment may undertake leverage:
questions.option_A: Never — SPVs must be unleveraged
questions.option_B: As disclosed in the placement memorandum
questions.option_C: Up to 2x NAV as a hard cap
questions.option_D: Only with case-by-case IFSCA approval
questions.correct_text: As disclosed in the placement memorandum
questions.explanation: Reg. 41(3): SPV leverage is a disclosure matter — permitted to the extent the PPM discloses it. The framework consistently prefers disclosed flexibility over hard caps for sophisticated-investor products.

questions.question: For a restricted scheme — is this the current legal position or the pre-amendment position?
questions.explanation: Pre-amendment. Since 30.01.2026, restricted schemes have the multi-extension regime: successive 6-month extensions, application filed while the PPM is still valid, 25% fee for the first and 50% for each subsequent extension.

questions.question: The 25% cap on unlisted securities for open-ended restricted schemes does NOT apply where:
questions.option_A: The scheme has more than five hundred investors on its register at the relevant point in time
questions.option_B: The unlisted securities are those of companies incorporated within the IFSC and nowhere else
questions.option_C: An open-ended fund of funds invests in open-ended schemes that keep unlisted exposure within 25% of corpus
questions.option_D: The FME furnishes the Authority with a quarterly undertaking confirming its continued compliance
questions.correct_text: An open-ended fund of funds invests in open-ended schemes that keep unlisted exposure within 25% of corpus
questions.explanation: Reg. 35(1) proviso: the FoF look-through — if the underlying open-ended schemes each respect the 25% limit, the FoF layer is exempt from re-testing it.

questions.question: Module 4 — Restricted Numbers Deck
How many compliance failures can you count?
questions.option_A: None — nineteen working days is sufficient and trustee approval is indeed not required here
questions.option_B: One — only the filing timeline falls short of what the regulation actually requires
questions.option_C: Two — the filing timeline and the deferred incorporation of the Authority's comments
questions.option_D: Three — the timeline, the deferred comments, and the missing fiduciary approval are all breaches.
questions.correct_text: Three — the timeline, the deferred comments, and the missing fiduciary approval are all breaches.

questions.question: A retail scheme's draft offer document must be filed with IFSCA at least:
questions.option_A: Twenty-one (21) working days before the launch of the scheme
questions.option_B: Fourteen (14) calendar days before the launch of the scheme
questions.option_C: Thirty (30) working days before the launch of the scheme
questions.option_D: Seven (7) working days before the launch of the scheme
questions.correct_text: Twenty-one (21) working days before the launch of the scheme
questions.explanation: Reg. 43(1): 21 working days, with applicable fees. Contrast with the private-placement green channel for VC/restricted schemes, where subscription can open immediately on taken-on-record.

questions.question: The validity of a retail scheme's offer document is:
questions.option_A: Six (6) months from the date the document is filed with IFSCA
questions.option_B: Twelve (12) months from IFSCA's taken-on-record communication
questions.option_C: Twenty-four (24) months from the launch date of the scheme
questions.option_D: Perpetual, subject only to annual updation by the FME
questions.correct_text: Twelve (12) months from IFSCA's taken-on-record communication
questions.explanation: Twelve months from taken-on-record — the same validity clock as VC and restricted scheme PPMs. The communication also serves as the Certificate of Registration for Income Tax Act purposes.

questions.question: A retail scheme must have:
questions.option_A: At least 50 investors, with no single investor exceeding 10% of the corpus of the scheme at any time
questions.option_B: At least 20 investors from the very first day of the offer, with no cure period at all
questions.option_C: At least 20 investors with no single investor exceeding 25%, achieved within 6 months of closure of the offer
questions.option_D: At least 100 investors, with no concentration limit applying to any single investor
questions.correct_text: At least 20 investors with no single investor exceeding 25%, achieved within 6 months of closure of the offer
questions.explanation: Reg. 44: minimum 20 investors, 25% single-investor cap, with a 6-month post-closure window to achieve compliance. The cure period is the detail exams isolate.

questions.question: A retail scheme in IFSC must be constituted as:
questions.option_A: A Company, an LLP or a Trust, at the option of the FME
questions.option_B: Only a Trust settled under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882
questions.option_C: Any form, including a variable capital company
questions.option_D: A Company or a Trust under the applicable laws of India
questions.correct_text: A Company or a Trust under the applicable laws of India
questions.explanation: Reg. 45(4): company or trust only. The LLP option — available for the FME entity itself and various restricted structures — is absent for retail schemes.

questions.question: The tenure of a close-ended retail scheme may be extended up to 2 years with:
questions.option_A: Approval of two-thirds of investors by value AND the approval of the Authority
questions.option_B: Approval of two-thirds of the investors by value, without any further approval
questions.option_C: Approval of the Authority alone, no investor resolution being required at all
questions.option_D: Approval of a simple majority of the investors counted by number, not value
questions.correct_text: Approval of two-thirds of investors by value AND the approval of the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 45(3): retail extensions need both the 2/3-by-value investor vote and IFSCA approval — the extra Authority layer distinguishes retail from restricted/VC schemes, where investor approval suffices.

questions.question: A retail scheme may be filed with the Authority only if:
questions.option_A: The FME board alone has approved it
questions.option_B: It has been approved by the fiduciaries
questions.option_C: IFSCA has pre-cleared the investment strategy
questions.option_D: The scheme has secured anchor investors
questions.correct_text: It has been approved by the fiduciaries
questions.explanation: Reg. 43(5): fiduciary approval (board of the scheme-company / trustees) is a precondition to filing itself. It cannot be ratified after the fact.

questions.question: An FME intending to launch retail schemes must, for appointing any person as a fiduciary:
questions.option_A: Merely intimate the Authority within 15 days
questions.option_B: Obtain investor consent at the first general meeting
questions.option_C: Take prior approval of the Authority
questions.option_D: Nothing — fiduciary appointments are unregulated
questions.correct_text: Take prior approval of the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 17(4): retail fiduciary appointments need prior IFSCA approval — for non-retail schemes, fiduciaries need only meet fit-and-proper standards without pre-approval.

questions.question: Retail schemes may be structured as:
questions.option_A: Open-ended schemes only
questions.option_B: Close-ended schemes only
questions.option_C: Interval schemes only, with defined transaction periods
questions.option_D: Either open-ended or close-ended
questions.correct_text: Either open-ended or close-ended
questions.explanation: Reg. 45(1): both structures are available. Close-ended retail schemes carry a minimum 3-year tenure disclosed in the offer document.

questions.question: Module 5 — Retail Numbers Deck
A special situation fund is a scheme that invests in special situation assets and may additionally:
questions.option_A: Act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
questions.option_B: Underwrite public issues of equity securities made by its investee companies
questions.option_C: Provide bridge loans to its own fund management entity on arm's length terms
questions.option_D: Act as an insolvency professional in proceedings before the Tribunal itself
questions.correct_text: Act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
questions.explanation: The SSF definition twins distressed-asset investing with eligibility to bid as a resolution applicant under the IBC — the regulatory bridge between IFSC capital and Indian insolvency resolution.

questions.question: A special situation fund must be:
questions.option_A: Open-ended only, with redemption available to investors at defined intervals throughout
questions.option_B: Close-ended only, with a tenure of not less than three (3) years disclosed in the placement memorandum
questions.option_C: Either open-ended or close-ended, at the option of the fund management entity concerned
questions.option_D: Close-ended only, with a minimum tenure of five (5) years running from the first close
questions.correct_text: Close-ended only, with a tenure of not less than three (3) years disclosed in the placement memorandum
questions.explanation: Reg. 56: close-ended only, minimum 3-year tenure. Distressed strategies need locked capital; redemption liquidity is structurally incompatible.

questions.question: A special situation fund may be launched by:
questions.option_A: Only a Registered FME (Retail), through an offer document filed with the Authority
questions.option_B: Any Authorised FME, provided that its net worth meets the prescribed minimum
questions.option_C: A Registered FME, through a private placement memorandum filed with the Authority
questions.option_D: Only banks and non-banking financial companies operating within the IFSC
questions.correct_text: A Registered FME, through a private placement memorandum filed with the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 55(1): Registered FMEs launch SSFs by private placement. Authorised FMEs — limited to VC schemes and FIFs — cannot.

questions.question: The filing of an SSF placement memorandum follows:
questions.option_A: A 21-working-day prior review by the Authority, exactly as for retail schemes
questions.option_B: A 30-working-day public comment process before any subscription may open at all
questions.option_C: Case-by-case approval by the Authority before any subscription may be accepted
questions.option_D: The green channel — open for subscription immediately upon taken-on-record communication
questions.correct_text: The green channel — open for subscription immediately upon taken-on-record communication
questions.explanation: SSFs share the private-placement green channel: subscription opens on taken-on-record, with IFSCA retaining the right to comment at any stage for incorporation.

questions.question: If an SSF misses its minimum corpus within PPM validity, the extension available is:
questions.option_A: A one-time option to extend by 6 months, paying 50% of the fresh-scheme filing fee
questions.option_B: Multiple six-month extensions at 25% and 50% fees, as for restricted schemes
questions.option_C: No extension whatsoever; the placement memorandum simply lapses on expiry
questions.option_D: An automatic twelve-month grace period requiring no further filing at all
questions.correct_text: A one-time option to extend by 6 months, paying 50% of the fresh-scheme filing fee
questions.explanation: Reg. 55(3) was untouched by the 2026 Amendment: SSFs remain on the one-time, 6-month, 50%-fee regime while VC and restricted schemes moved to multi-extension. The asymmetry is deliberate exam bait.

questions.question: Extension of an SSF's tenure beyond the initial 2-year extension requires:
questions.option_A: A fresh two-thirds vote of the investors by value at the end of each financial year
questions.option_B: Express consent of willing investors, with an exit opportunity for dissenting investors
questions.option_C: The approval of the Authority alone, without any reference to the investors
questions.option_D: Nothing further, since extension beyond that point is prohibited absolutely
questions.correct_text: Express consent of willing investors, with an exit opportunity for dissenting investors
questions.explanation: The ladder: up to 2 years on a 2/3-by-value vote; beyond that, only willing investors stay and dissenters must be offered an exit. Consent replaces majority coercion at the far end.

questions.question: The SSF placement memorandum is valid for:
questions.option_A: Six (6) months from the date of filing with the Authority, without any extension
questions.option_B: Eighteen (18) months from the launch of the scheme through to its first close
questions.option_C: Twelve (12) months from the taken-on-record communication, within which first close must be declared
questions.option_D: Until the first drawdown of capital is made from the committed investors alike
questions.correct_text: Twelve (12) months from the taken-on-record communication, within which first close must be declared
questions.explanation: The standard 12-month validity applies; first close requires achieving the minimum corpus under Reg. 58(1) within that window (or the one-time extension).

questions.question: Module 6 — SSF Deck
Exchange Traded Funds in IFSC may be launched by:
questions.option_A: Any Registered FME
questions.option_B: Authorised FMEs with Authority approval
questions.option_C: Recognised stock exchanges directly
questions.option_D: Only Registered FMEs (Retail)
questions.correct_text: Only Registered FMEs (Retail)
questions.explanation: Reg. 61(1): ETFs sit exclusively in the Retail tier — consistent with their public, exchange-traded nature. Filing follows the retail pattern: draft offer document 21 working days before launch.

questions.question: The ETF offer document must be filed at least ____ before launch, with validity of ____:
questions.option_A: 21 working days; 12 months from taken-on-record
questions.option_B: 30 working days; 6 months from the date of filing
questions.option_C: 14 working days; 12 months from the launch date
questions.option_D: 21 calendar days; 24 months from taken-on-record
questions.correct_text: 21 working days; 12 months from taken-on-record
questions.explanation: Same discipline as retail schemes: 21-working-day prior filing, 12-month validity, comments incorporated pre-launch, material changes reported immediately.

questions.question: An ETF launched in IFSC:
questions.option_A: May be listed at the option of the fund management entity concerned
questions.option_B: Must be mandatorily listed and traded on a recognised stock exchange
questions.option_C: Must be listed only where its assets under management exceed USD 50 Million
questions.option_D: Trades exclusively over-the-counter between authorised participants
questions.correct_text: Must be mandatorily listed and traded on a recognised stock exchange
questions.explanation: Reg. 61(5): listing is mandatory — an unlisted ETF is a contradiction the regulations do not permit. The exchange itself becomes a second gatekeeper for novel ETF types.

questions.question: A "Hybrid ETF" under the regulations is one that:
questions.option_A: Combines active and passive strategies in one fund
questions.option_B: Lists on two or more exchanges
questions.option_C: Invests in two or more asset classes
questions.option_D: Holds both physical and derivative gold
questions.correct_text: Invests in two or more asset classes
questions.explanation: The permitted menu: Equity Index, Debt Index, Commodity-based, Hybrid (2+ asset classes), Actively Managed, and others subject to approval of the exchange and the Authority. Note that actively managed ETFs are expressly permitted.

questions.question: A Gold ETF must invest at least ____ of AUM in gold or bullion instruments, with ETCD exposure capped at ____:
questions.option_D: 90%; 10% of AUM
questions.correct_text: 90%; 10% of AUM
questions.explanation: Reg. 65(1): ≥90% in gold/bullion instruments (including Bullion Depository Receipts with gold underlying); gold-ETCD exposure ≤10% of AUM.

questions.question: Physical gold underlying a Gold ETF must be:
questions.option_A: Stored with a vault registered with the Authority, and physically verified half-yearly by an independent agency within two months
questions.option_B: Stored with any scheduled commercial bank in India, and physically verified once each year by the fund management entity itself
questions.option_C: Held by the FME itself at its own premises within the IFSC, and verified annually by its own statutory auditor
questions.option_D: Held with an overseas bullion bank of repute, and physically verified each quarter by the appointed custodian
questions.correct_text: Stored with a vault registered with the Authority, and physically verified half-yearly by an independent agency within two months
questions.explanation: Two safeguards: Authority-registered vault custody, plus independent half-yearly physical verification reported to the FME and fiduciaries within two months of each half-year.

questions.question: A Silver ETF must invest at least ____ of AUM in silver or silver bullion instruments:
questions.option_A: 75%, with the balance 25% available for other instruments
questions.option_B: 90%, with silver-ETCD exposure not exceeding 10% of AUM
questions.option_C: 95%, with no exposure to silver-linked derivatives permitted
questions.option_D: 80%, with up to 20% held in gold for diversification purposes
questions.correct_text: 90%, with silver-ETCD exposure not exceeding 10% of AUM
questions.explanation: Reg. 66(1) mirrors the gold architecture for silver: ≥90% in silver/bullion instruments (including BDRs with silver underlying), ETCD exposure ≤10%.

questions.question: A "fund of funds scheme" invests in other schemes (in IFSC, India or foreign jurisdictions), except to the extent of funds needed for:
questions.option_A: Up to 49% of the corpus may be invested directly in the securities of listed and unlisted companies
questions.option_B: Seed investments made in new schemes launched by its own FME, as disclosed to the investors
questions.option_C: Meeting expenses, hedging, or liquidity for repurchases, redemptions and distributions, as disclosed in the PPM
questions.option_D: Any purpose approved by the fiduciaries of the scheme and duly recorded in their minutes
questions.correct_text: Meeting expenses, hedging, or liquidity for repurchases, redemptions and distributions, as disclosed in the PPM
questions.explanation: The definitional carve-outs are narrow and disclosure-bound: expenses, hedging, and redemption/distribution liquidity. Beyond those, a FoF holds schemes — not direct securities.

questions.question: The independent-valuation requirement does not apply to a fund of funds scheme where:
questions.option_A: Its assets under management remain below USD 10 Million as at the end of every financial year of the scheme
questions.option_B: All of its investors are accredited investors within the meaning of these regulations, without exception
questions.option_C: The FME undertakes an internal valuation of the scheme's assets at the end of every quarter
questions.option_D: It invests in schemes regulated by a financial sector regulator that are themselves valued by an independent entity
questions.correct_text: It invests in schemes regulated by a financial sector regulator that are themselves valued by an independent entity
questions.explanation: The look-through principle: if the underlying regulated schemes already carry independent valuation, re-valuing them at the FoF layer adds cost without protection.

questions.question: Module 7 — ETF/FoF Deck
An Investment Trust (REIT/InvIT) raising funds by private placement must raise from:
questions.option_A: Investors investing at least USD 250,000 or accredited investors, capped at fifty (50) investors
questions.option_B: Any investors at all, subject only to an overall cap of two hundred (200) investors
questions.option_C: Institutional investors only, subject to an overall cap of one thousand investors
questions.option_D: Accredited investors only, with no cap at all on the number of such investors
questions.correct_text: Investors investing at least USD 250,000 or accredited investors, capped at fifty (50) investors
questions.explanation: Reg. 93: the private-placement gate is USD 250,000 / accredited status, with a 50-investor ceiling — the same sophistication thresholds as VC schemes.

questions.question: After a private placement, the Investment Trust must file the final placement memorandum with the Authority within:
questions.option_A: Five (5) working days from the closure of the placement
questions.option_B: Ten (10) working days from the date of allotment of units
questions.option_C: Thirty (30) days from the date of allotment of units
questions.option_D: Before any allotment of units can lawfully occur
questions.correct_text: Ten (10) working days from the date of allotment of units
questions.explanation: Reg. 93(d): final PM within 10 working days of allotment — a post-completion filing, unlike the pre-launch review that governs public issues.

questions.question: For a public issue, the Investment Trust (through its IM or investment banker) files the draft offer document:
questions.option_A: Twenty-one (21) working days before the listing of the units on the recognised stock exchange
questions.option_B: Ten (10) working days before the issue opens for subscription by the investors concerned
questions.option_C: Not less than thirty (30) working days before filing the offer document with the exchange and the Authority
questions.option_D: Simultaneously with the filing that is made with the recognised stock exchange itself
questions.correct_text: Not less than thirty (30) working days before filing the offer document with the exchange and the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 94(b): the 30-working-day runway precedes the formal offer document filing — creating space for the public comment and observation process.

questions.question: The draft offer document of a public issue must be hosted for public comments for:
questions.option_A: Seven (7) days, on the website of the Authority alone and on no other website
questions.option_B: Twenty-one (21) working days, on the website of the recognised stock exchange only
questions.option_C: Thirty (30) days, by advertisement published in two national daily newspapers
questions.option_D: Not less than fourteen (14) days, on the websites of the Authority, exchange(s), investment manager and bankers
questions.correct_text: Not less than fourteen (14) days, on the websites of the Authority, exchange(s), investment manager and bankers
questions.explanation: Reg. 94(c): a minimum 14-day public exposure across four sets of websites — the crowdsourced layer of due diligence unique to public offers.

questions.question: The draft offer document and offer document must be accompanied by a due diligence certificate signed by:
questions.option_A: The investment manager or the investment banker, as the case may be
questions.option_B: The trustees of the Investment Trust, acting on behalf of unit holders
questions.option_C: The statutory auditor of the Investment Trust for the relevant year
questions.option_D: The board of directors of the sponsor of the Investment Trust
questions.correct_text: The investment manager or the investment banker, as the case may be
questions.explanation: Reg. 94(d): the IM or investment banker personally certifies diligence — placing professional accountability behind the disclosure document.

questions.question: IFSCA communicates its observations on a public-issue offer document within:
questions.option_A: A fixed thirty (30) calendar days running from the date of the original filing
questions.option_B: 30 working days from filing, or 21 working days from satisfactory reply to queries — whichever is later
questions.option_C: Fifteen (15) working days from the close of the public comment period itself
questions.option_D: Sixty (60) days from the filing, extendable once at the Authority's discretion
questions.correct_text: 30 working days from filing, or 21 working days from satisfactory reply to queries — whichever is later
questions.explanation: Reg. 94(e): the "whichever is later" formulation means the clock restarts with each round of queries — incomplete responses extend, not shorten, the timeline.

questions.question: The offer document must be filed with the recognised stock exchange(s) and the Authority:
questions.option_A: On the very day that the offer opens for subscription by investors
questions.option_B: Ten (10) working days before the opening of the offer for subscription
questions.option_C: Not less than five (5) working days before the opening of the offer
questions.option_D: Within five (5) working days after the opening of the offer
questions.correct_text: Not less than five (5) working days before the opening of the offer
questions.explanation: Reg. 94(g): a 5-working-day pre-opening buffer with the final document — the last checkpoint before public money moves.

questions.question: If the initial offer, follow-on or rights issue is not made within one (1) year from the date of IFSCA's observations:
questions.option_A: The observations extend automatically for six months
questions.option_B: The issue may proceed with a confirmatory letter
questions.option_C: The Trust is deregistered
questions.option_D: A fresh draft offer document must be filed
questions.correct_text: A fresh draft offer document must be filed
questions.explanation: Reg. 94(h): observations have a 12-month shelf life. Market disclosures go stale; a lapsed window means restarting the full draft-and-observation cycle.

questions.question: Module 8 — Investment Trust Deck
An independent custodian must be appointed for:
questions.option_A: Retail schemes; open-ended restricted schemes; and other schemes with AUM above USD 70 Million
questions.option_B: All schemes without any exception at all, whatever their size or investor base
questions.option_C: Only retail schemes, since all other schemes are for sophisticated investors
questions.option_D: Only those schemes holding physical commodities such as gold or silver bullion
questions.correct_text: Retail schemes; open-ended restricted schemes; and other schemes with AUM above USD 70 Million
questions.explanation: Reg. 132's trio: retail (investor protection), open-ended restricted (redemption integrity), and any scheme above USD 70M AUM (systemic size).

questions.question: The custodian requirement is not mandatory for a fund of funds scheme where:
questions.option_A: Its assets under management remain below the USD 70 Million threshold
questions.option_B: The underlying scheme(s) have appointed independent custodian(s)
questions.option_C: All of the investors have consented to the arrangement in writing
questions.option_D: The FME provides an indemnity to the investors of the scheme
questions.correct_text: The underlying scheme(s) have appointed independent custodian(s)
questions.explanation: Look-through again: if the assets are already in independent custody at the underlying level, duplicating custody at the FoF layer is redundant.

questions.question: The custodian appointed under Reg. 132 must be based in IFSC, unless:
questions.option_A: The parent of the fund management entity is a foreign bank regulated in its home jurisdiction and the securities are held there
questions.option_B: The scheme invests only in securities listed on Indian stock exchanges, in which case an India-regulated custodian may be appointed
questions.option_C: Local law where the securities are issued mandates a local custodian — a custodian regulated in that jurisdiction may then be appointed for them
questions.option_D: The custodian fee payable would exceed the cap specified by the Authority, in which case a foreign custodian may be appointed instead
questions.correct_text: Local law where the securities are issued mandates a local custodian — a custodian regulated in that jurisdiction may then be appointed for them
questions.explanation: Explanation I: IFSC-domicile is the default; the carve-out follows mandatory local-custody laws of the issuing jurisdiction, with information arrangements for IFSCA.

questions.question: Schemes required to appoint an IFSC-based custodian may make that appointment within:
questions.option_A: Six (6) months from the launch of the scheme, using any independent custodian in the interim
questions.option_B: Twelve (12) months from the taken-on-record date, with no interim arrangement permitted
questions.option_C: No transition at all — IFSC-based custody applies from the very first day of the scheme
questions.option_D: 24 months from commencement of the 2026 Amendment, using an India/foreign-regulated custodian in the interim
questions.correct_text: 24 months from commencement of the 2026 Amendment, using an India/foreign-regulated custodian in the interim
questions.explanation: The substituted Explanation II (w.e.f. 30.01.2026) gives a 24-month runway with interim custody permitted through regulated custodians in India or foreign jurisdictions.

questions.question: Scheme assets must be valued in line with norms in the ____ by ____:
questions.option_A: Sixth Schedule; an independent service provider (fund administrator, custodian, registered CRA or IBBI-registered valuer)
questions.option_B: The Third Schedule; by the internal audit team of the FME, reviewed by its statutory auditor
questions.option_C: The Fifth Schedule; by any chartered accountant in practice appointed by the FME each year
questions.option_D: The Second Schedule; by the statutory auditor of the scheme for the relevant financial year
questions.correct_text: Sixth Schedule; an independent service provider (fund administrator, custodian, registered CRA or IBBI-registered valuer)
questions.explanation: Valuation norms live in the Sixth Schedule; execution belongs to the listed independents. The FME and fiduciaries carry the compliance obligation jointly.

questions.question: A FoF investing in regulator-supervised schemes that are independently valued:
questions.option_A: Must still appoint its own IBBI-registered valuer for the purpose
questions.option_B: Is exempt from the independent-valuation requirement at the FoF level
questions.option_C: Must value its assets on a monthly basis rather than an annual one
questions.option_D: Loses its classification as a fund of funds scheme altogether
questions.correct_text: Is exempt from the independent-valuation requirement at the FoF level
questions.explanation: Where underlying schemes are regulated and independently valued, the FoF layer inherits that integrity rather than re-purchasing it.

questions.question: For Venture Capital schemes, NAV must be computed:
questions.option_A: Daily, and published each day on the website of the fund management entity
questions.option_B: Quarterly, and certified by the custodian appointed for the scheme concerned
questions.option_C: At least annually, with the procedure and methodology fully documented and regularly verified
questions.option_D: Only when an investor makes a specific written request for the valuation
questions.correct_text: At least annually, with the procedure and methodology fully documented and regularly verified
questions.explanation: Annual minimum plus documentation discipline. Portfolio disclosure to investors follows separately — at least yearly, within one month of financial year end.

questions.question: The scheme annual report must be submitted to the Authority, and its abridged summary shared with investors, within:
questions.option_A: Three months to the Authority, and six months to the investors in the scheme concerned
questions.option_B: Six months for both the filing with the Authority and the summary sent to investors
questions.option_C: Sixty days for both the Authority filing and the summary shared with the investors
questions.option_D: Four months from the financial year end — with the full report supplied within 15 days of any investor request
questions.correct_text: Four months from the financial year end — with the full report supplied within 15 days of any investor request
questions.explanation: Reg. 134: a single 4-month clock for both the Authority submission and the investor summary; the full report is on-demand within 15 days.

questions.question: The annual statement of accounts of every scheme must be audited by an auditor who:
questions.option_A: Is not in any way associated with the FME
questions.option_B: Is empanelled with the Authority
questions.option_C: Rotates every three years
questions.option_D: Is the same auditor as the FME's statutory auditor
questions.correct_text: Is not in any way associated with the FME
questions.explanation: Reg. 135(1): total dissociation from the FME — a stricter formulation than mere "independence" tests, closing side-relationship loopholes.

questions.question: Module 9 — Custody & Valuation Deck
Before filing a scheme document, the FME must appoint fiduciaries as follows:
questions.option_A: A single independent fiduciary, whatever legal form the FME has adopted for itself in the IFSC
questions.option_B: Board of Directors (company); Designated Partners (LLP); Trustees, including a trustee company's board
questions.option_C: Observers nominated by the Authority to sit on the board of each of the FME's schemes
questions.option_D: A compliance committee comprising three of the key managerial personnel of the FME
questions.correct_text: Board of Directors (company); Designated Partners (LLP); Trustees, including a trustee company's board
questions.explanation: Reg. 17(2): the fiduciary layer maps to legal form — BoD, DPs or Trustees. All must satisfy fit-and-proper standards, and retail fiduciaries need prior Authority approval.

questions.question: Fiduciaries must comply with the Code of Conduct and obligations detailed in:
questions.option_A: Part A of the Second Schedule
questions.option_B: The Fifth Schedule
questions.option_C: Part B of the Third Schedule
questions.option_D: Each scheme's placement memorandum only
questions.correct_text: Part B of the Third Schedule
questions.explanation: Third Schedule architecture: Part A is the FME's code; Part B belongs to the fiduciaries. Both operate alongside scheme-level documents.

questions.question: An FME's Investment Committee is:
questions.option_A: Mandatory for every Registered FME, whatever the size of the assets it has under management and whatever the scheme type
questions.option_B: Mandatory only where the assets under management of the FME exceed USD 1 billion as at each financial year end
questions.option_C: Prohibited in the case of retail schemes, because the fiduciaries of the scheme already perform that function
questions.option_D: Discretionary — but if constituted, its members must also comply with the responsibilities cast on the FME and fund managers
questions.correct_text: Discretionary — but if constituted, its members must also comply with the responsibilities cast on the FME and fund managers
questions.explanation: Reg. 129: constituting an IC is the FME's choice, but membership imports personal regulatory responsibility — the committee is no liability shield.

questions.question: Scheme fees and expenses must be:
questions.option_A: Identified and appropriated separately per scheme, with maximum fees and each expense disclosed as a line item in the offer document
questions.option_B: Aggregated at the level of the FME and then allocated across all of its schemes once in each financial year, on a reasonable basis
questions.option_C: Capped at 2% of the assets under management by the regulations themselves, whatever the type or size of the scheme concerned
questions.option_D: Disclosed only to the fiduciaries of the scheme and not to its investors, who see only the net returns after all charges
questions.correct_text: Identified and appropriated separately per scheme, with maximum fees and each expense disclosed as a line item in the offer document
questions.explanation: Reg. 128: no pooling across schemes, no bundled expense lines. Maximums and per-item disclosure go into the offering document — investors price the drag upfront.

questions.question: FME advertisements must conform to:
questions.option_A: The Third Schedule Code of Conduct
questions.option_B: The Advertisement Code specified in the Fifth Schedule
questions.option_C: SEBI's advertisement code, applied mutatis mutandis
questions.option_D: No specific code — general fair-dealing principles only
questions.correct_text: The Advertisement Code specified in the Fifth Schedule
questions.explanation: Reg. 127 points to the Fifth Schedule Advertisement Code — the dedicated standard for FME marketing communications.

questions.question: Merger, demerger or restructuring of schemes requires:
questions.option_A: A two-thirds vote of the investors by value, without any further approval at all
questions.option_B: The approval of the fiduciaries of each of the schemes concerned, and nothing more
questions.option_C: Compliance with conditions specified by the Authority AND prior approval by the Authority
questions.option_D: Only a post-facto intimation to the Authority once the merger has been completed
questions.correct_text: Compliance with conditions specified by the Authority AND prior approval by the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 130: double lock — specified conditions plus prior Authority approval. Scheme-level corporate actions cannot proceed on investor consent alone.

questions.question: Under the FME Code of Conduct, the Chief Executive Officer (whatever the designation) must ensure:
questions.option_A: Only the accuracy of the financial statements prepared for the FME and for each of its schemes separately
questions.option_B: Only the redressal of investor grievances received in relation to the schemes under management
questions.option_C: Only that all marketing material complies with the applicable advertisement code and disclosures
questions.option_D: Compliance with the regulations, that investments serve unit holders' interests, and the overall risk management function
questions.correct_text: Compliance with the regulations, that investments serve unit holders' interests, and the overall risk management function
questions.explanation: Part A(d): the CEO personally owns regulatory compliance, investor-interest alignment of investments, and overall risk management — irrespective of internal delegation.

questions.question: Under the Code of Conduct, the FME, its directors, partners and officers:
questions.option_A: Are not absolved of liability to the scheme or investors for acts of commission or omission — notwithstanding any contract or termination
questions.option_B: Are released from all liability on resignation, provided that thirty days' notice has been duly given
questions.option_C: May contract out of that liability with the written consent of the scheme's investors obtained in advance
questions.option_D: Are liable only for so long as they continue to hold office within the FME or the scheme concerned
questions.correct_text: Are not absolved of liability to the scheme or investors for acts of commission or omission — notwithstanding any contract or termination
questions.explanation: The Code pierces both contract and exit: liability for acts while in office survives termination and cannot be waived by agreement. The FME is also responsible for acts of its employees and procured personnel.

questions.question: Module 10 — Governance Deck
The FME must provide investors information about their holdings in its schemes:
questions.option_A: Quarterly, and within thirty days of any request that an investor makes
questions.option_B: At the end of every month, and within ten working days of any investor request
questions.option_C: Annually only, through the annual report that is circulated to investors
questions.option_D: Only through the annual report, with no obligation to respond to requests
questions.correct_text: At the end of every month, and within ten working days of any investor request
questions.explanation: Reg. 136(1): monthly statements as the baseline, with a 10-working-day response clock for ad hoc requests. Fiduciaries separately must disclose anything with an adverse bearing on investments.

questions.question: An FME may undertake business activities other than those specified in the regulations:
questions.option_A: Freely, if conducted through a subsidiary
questions.option_B: With 30 days' advance intimation
questions.option_C: Only with prior approval of the Authority
questions.option_D: Never, under any circumstances
questions.correct_text: Only with prior approval of the Authority
questions.explanation: Reg. 137: activity perimeter is closed by default, openable only by prior IFSCA approval — not intimation, not disclosure.

questions.question: An FME operating as a branch that obtains a sectoral-regulator approval at its principal place of operations for an activity outside IFSC must:
questions.option_A: Seek fresh IFSCA approval before acting on it
questions.option_B: Do nothing — it is outside IFSCA's remit
questions.option_C: Publish the approval on its website
questions.option_D: Inform the Authority within fifteen (15) days
questions.correct_text: Inform the Authority within fifteen (15) days
questions.explanation: First proviso to Reg. 137: 15-day notification. Separately, opening marketing/client-service branches in other jurisdictions requires prior intimation to IFSCA with details.

questions.question: IFSCA may appoint an Inspecting Authority:
questions.option_A: Suo motu, or upon receipt of information or complaint, at any time
questions.option_B: Only after first issuing a show-cause notice to the FME concerned
questions.option_C: Only annually, in accordance with a published inspection calendar
questions.option_D: Only on the direction of a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction
questions.correct_text: Suo motu, or upon receipt of information or complaint, at any time
questions.explanation: Reg. 138(1): inspection needs no external trigger — the Authority may move on its own motion, on information, or on complaint, at any time.

questions.question: The inspection may cover the FME's:
questions.option_A: The financial statements of the FME and of each of the schemes that it manages, and nothing else
questions.option_B: Books, accounts, records, documents, infrastructure, procedures and systems — and associated entities
questions.option_C: Only the records of those schemes that manage assets above the USD 70 Million threshold
questions.option_D: Only those documents which post-date the complaint on which the inspection was ordered
questions.correct_text: Books, accounts, records, documents, infrastructure, procedures and systems — and associated entities
questions.explanation: The scope is total — extending beyond the FME to associated entities, and to the affairs of schemes and activities under the regulations.

questions.question: During an inspection, the duty to assist and furnish records binds:
questions.option_A: Only the Principal Officer and the Compliance Officer of the FME that is under inspection
questions.option_B: Only the board of directors of the FME, acting collectively rather than individually
questions.option_C: The FME and every officer, partner, trustee, director, chairperson, CEO, KMP, employee and agent of the FME
questions.option_D: Only those employees who have been specifically named in the inspection order itself
questions.correct_text: The FME and every officer, partner, trustee, director, chairperson, CEO, KMP, employee and agent of the FME
questions.explanation: Reg. 139 casts the cooperation net over everyone — including agents — with reasonable access to premises and records within the Inspecting Authority's timelines.

questions.question: Investors may wind up a scheme by resolution passed by:
questions.option_A: A simple majority of the investors, counted by number rather than by value
questions.option_B: Two-thirds of the investors by value of their investment in that scheme
questions.option_C: Ninety per cent (90%) of the investors by value at a meeting of investors
questions.option_D: Seventy-five per cent (75%) of investors by value, at a meeting of the investors
questions.correct_text: Seventy-five per cent (75%) of investors by value, at a meeting of the investors
questions.explanation: Reg. 131(1)(b): the 75%-by-value supermajority again — the same threshold that governs associate transactions. Tenure expiry under (a) and the new voluntary route under (c) are the other grounds.

questions.question: In the interest of investors and orderly market development, the Authority may direct an FME to:
questions.option_A: Wind up a scheme, merge certain schemes, or manage schemes of other FMEs
questions.option_B: Suspend fresh subscriptions into the scheme, and nothing beyond that
questions.option_C: Appoint an administrator to manage the scheme in place of the FME
questions.option_D: Impose monetary penalties on the FME and its key managerial personnel
questions.correct_text: Wind up a scheme, merge certain schemes, or manage schemes of other FMEs
questions.explanation: Reg. 131(2): three directive powers — including the striking power to order one FME to manage another FME's schemes, IFSC's resolution mechanism for failing managers.

questions.question: The ground inserted by the 2026 Amendment permits winding up where:
questions.option_A: The net asset value of the scheme falls by fifty per cent within a single quarter, measured against the previous quarter end
questions.option_B: Funds were raised but the minimum corpus was missed within the (extended) PPM validity, and the FME did not extend it by filing and paying the fee
questions.option_C: The custodian appointed for the scheme resigns and no replacement custodian is appointed within the prescribed period
questions.option_D: Two consecutive annual reports of the scheme carry a qualified opinion from the statutory auditor
questions.correct_text: Funds were raised but the minimum corpus was missed within the (extended) PPM validity, and the FME did not extend it by filing and paying the fee
questions.explanation: Reg. 131(1)(c) (w.e.f. 30.01.2026) pairs with the new multi-extension regime: where a raise falls short and the FME has NOT filed for a further extension, there is now a clean statutory exit. The same amendment also inserted Reg. 131(1)(d) — a separate ground for winding up where NO investors have been onboarded and NO funds collected, and the FME voluntarily desires to wind up. Keep the two apart: (c) is a failed raise; (d) is a scheme that never started.

questions.question: Module 11 — Oversight Deck
What's wrong here?
questions.option_A: Nothing is wrong — the extension is valid, since a one-time six-month extension at a 50% fee remains available
questions.option_B: Only the fee is wrong — it should have been 25% of the fresh-scheme filing fee for a first extension
questions.option_C: The application is fatally late — it had to be filed while the PPM was still valid — and the fee and the CO's position are outdated
questions.option_D: The scheme should simply have declared its first close at the USD 1.8 Million it had already raised
questions.correct_text: The application is fatally late — it had to be filed while the PPM was still valid — and the fee and the CO's position are outdated

questions.question: Is this the current legal position or the pre-amendment position?
questions.explanation: Current law. The 2026 Amendment substituted clause (b) of the KMP experience requirement and introduced graded routes: 5 years' experience in an "eligible institution" (a newly defined term), reduced to 3 years where the KMP holds a professional qualification, and a 2-year post-qualification route where the individual holds Authority-specified certifications. The pre-amendment text simply required 5 years in related securities-market activities.

questions.question: Is this the current legal position or the pre-amendment position?
questions.explanation: Pre-amendment. The 2026 Amendment substituted Explanation II to Reg. 132: schemes required to appoint an IFSC-based custodian now have a 24-month window from commencement of the Amendment (i.e., from 30.01.2026) to make that appointment, and may in the interim appoint an independent custodian in India or a foreign jurisdiction regulated by that jurisdiction's financial sector regulator.

questions.question: For a Venture Capital scheme — is this the current legal position or the pre-amendment position?
questions.explanation: Pre-amendment. For VC schemes, the 2026 Amendment substituted the Reg. 19(3) proviso with the multi-extension regime: successive 6-month extensions, application filed while the PPM is still valid, at 25% (first) / 50% (subsequent) of the prevailing fresh-scheme fee. Careful, though — this exact "one-time, 6 months, 50%" language IS still current law for Special Situation Funds under Reg. 55(3), which was not amended.

questions.question: Post the January 2026 Amendment, the fee for the FIRST extension of a restricted scheme's placement memorandum validity is:
questions.option_A: 50% of the applicable fee for filing a fresh scheme, as prevalent at the time
questions.option_B: 100% of the fee applicable to the filing of a fresh scheme with the Authority
questions.option_C: No fee at all, since the first extension is granted automatically on request
questions.option_D: 25% of the applicable fee for filing a fresh scheme, as prevalent at the time of extension
questions.correct_text: 25% of the applicable fee for filing a fresh scheme, as prevalent at the time of extension
questions.explanation: First extension: 25% of the prevailing fresh-scheme filing fee. Each subsequent extension: 50%. Note the words "as may be prevalent at the time of such extension" — the fee floats with the current fee schedule, not the fee paid at original filing.

questions.question: Under the current regime, each extension of a restricted scheme PPM runs for six months starting from:
questions.option_A: The day after expiry of the existing validity of the placement memorandum
questions.option_B: The date on which the extension application is filed with the Authority
questions.option_C: The date on which the Authority approves the extension application
questions.option_D: The date on which the scheme declares its first close to investors
questions.correct_text: The day after expiry of the existing validity of the placement memorandum
questions.explanation: Each extension is a 6-month period commencing the day after the existing validity expires — extensions stack back-to-back with no gaps. The application itself, however, must be filed while the PPM is still valid.

questions.question: An FME managing a Special Situation Fund misses first close within PPM validity. Its extension options are:
questions.option_A: Multiple 6-month extensions at 25%/50% fees — same as restricted schemes
questions.option_B: A one-time option to extend by 6 months at 50% of the fresh scheme filing fee
questions.option_C: Automatic 12-month extension on payment of 25% fee
questions.option_D: No extension is available for SSFs
questions.correct_text: A one-time option to extend by 6 months at 50% of the fresh scheme filing fee
questions.explanation: The trap: the January 2026 Amendment rewrote the extension regime for VC schemes (Reg. 19) and restricted schemes (Reg. 35), but did NOT touch Reg. 55(3) for Special Situation Funds. SSFs remain on the old one-time, 6-month, 50%-fee regime. Asymmetries created by amendments are prime examination territory.
